50:def deep_merge(base, override):
51-    """Return a new dict: ``base`` with ``override`` applied on top.
52-
53-    The merge is recursive. When the same key holds a mapping in *both*
54-    ``base`` and ``override``, the two mappings are merged key-by-key so that
55-    ``override`` wins at every individual leaf while values only present in
56-    ``base`` are preserved. For every other key, ``override`` replaces
57-    ``base`` outright. Neither input is mutated.
58-
59-    Example::
60-
61-        deep_merge(
62-            {"retry": {"max_attempts": 1, "backoff": "constant"}},
63-            {"retry": {"max_attempts": 3}},
64-        )
65-        # -> {"retry": {"max_attempts": 3, "backoff": "constant"}}
66-    """
67-
68-    result = dict(base)
69-    for key, value in override.items():
70-        if (
71-            key in result
72-            and isinstance(result[key], dict)
73-            and isinstance(value, dict)
74-        ):
75-            # Recurse with (base_child, override_child) so the override still
76-            # wins at the leaves while the base fills in the untouched keys.
77-            result[key] = deep_merge(value, result[key])
78-        else:
79-            result[key] = value
80-    return result
